name: Active Directory Security
tagline: Map, audit, and score Active Directory attack paths — graph enumeration, Kerberos/protocol tooling, credential-exposure testing, and risk health checks — for authorized assessments and blue-team defense.

tools.name: BloodHound CE
tools.desc: The current-generation attack-path engine: ingests SharpHound data into a Neo4j graph and reveals how users, groups, computers, sessions, GPOs, ACLs, trusts, and ADCS enrollments chain into paths to Domain Admin — including ADCS, NTLM, and delegation abuse conditions.
tools.when: The core analysis step after collection: visualize and triage which abusable identity relationships are the shortest paths to Tier-0, and why they matter to defenders.
tools.install: wget https://github.com/SpecterOps/bloodhound-cli/releases/latest/download/bloodhound-cli-linux-amd64.tar.gz (see the CE Quickstart for the Docker-Compose deployment)

tools.name: SharpHound
tools.desc: C# data collector for BloodHound CE that runs on domain-joined Windows and exports a zip of users, groups, sessions, local admins, ACLs, GPOs, trusts, and more via LDAP and SMB — the dataset the graph is built from.
tools.when: Run first from any authorized domain-joined host or as a standalone binary, then feed the output into BloodHound CE for graph analysis.
tools.install: Download the SharpHound CE binary from the BloodHound CE UI (Settings → Download Collectors) or the GitHub releases page

tools.name: PlumHound
tools.desc: Wraps BloodHound's Neo4j Cypher backend into repeatable HTML reports and task lists; surfaces the busiest paths to Domain Admin and which relationship to break to sever a given path.
tools.when: Turn a collected BloodHound graph into consumable, operations-ready findings for blue/purple-team remediation planning and scheduled reporting.

tools.name: Impacket
tools.desc: Fortra's Python library of Windows network protocol implementations plus ~100 example scripts — secretsdump (remote SAM/LSA/NTDS credential extraction over DRSUAPI/DCOM/registry in mimikatz-compatible hash format), psexec/wmiexec/atexec remote execution, ntlmrelayx, and a full Kerberos toolbox.
tools.when: The foundation for nearly all Linux-side AD work: secretsdump is the standard way to audit credential hygiene on controllers and hosts during an authorized assessment.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.desc: The maintained successor to CrackMapExec: multi-protocol (SMB, LDAP, MSSQL, SSH, WinRM, RDP) credential validation that rapidly tests which identities work where, sprays passwords, and enumerates shares, users, sessions, domains, and password policy across a fleet.
tools.when: Fast credential-driven health-check across many hosts in one pass — who is effective as admin, which policy is weakest, and which shares are open.

tools.name: Kerbrute
tools.desc: Go tool that validates AD usernames and tests passwords through Kerberos AS-REQ/AS-REP exchanges; its userenum mode never triggers account lockout, while passwordspray/bruteforce do and are meant for policy-aware testing.
tools.when: Discover which candidate usernames actually exist during recon, and safely prove a single reused weak password across a user list you monitor in your own logs.

tools.name: Rubeus
tools.desc: C# toolset for raw Kerberos interaction — ticket requests and passthe-ticket, overpass-the-hash, golden/silver/diamond ticket forging, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, and s4u delegation testing, compiled to run on Windows.
tools.when: Windows-side Kerberos validation: check which service accounts are Kerberoastable and how delegation and ticket caching expose lateral movement in your domain.
tools.install: Prebuilt binaries ship under Rubeus/Release — or compile with dotnet build against the repo source

tools.name: Mimikatz
tools.desc: The canonical Windows credential tool: sekurlsa extracts plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, PINs, and Kerberos tickets from LSASS memory, while lsadump covers SAM, LSA secrets, DCSync, and DCShadow, plus pass-the-hash/ticket and token manipulation.
tools.when: On an authorized host with local admin to prove whether LSASS-accessible credentials leak and whether protections like LSA Protection or Credential Guard actually hold.

tools.name: pypykatz
tools.desc: Pure-Python reimplementation of Mimikatz's sekurlsa: parses live LSASS memory or minidump files on any OS to recover NT hashes, plaintext credentials, Kerberos tickets, and DPAPI keys.
tools.when: Analyze an LSASS dump from Linux during incident response or assessment when you hold the dump rather than a live Windows host.

tools.name: lsassy
tools.desc: Python tool that remotely dumps LSASS (comsvcs, Procdump, nanodump, and more methods) over SMB/WMI from whole fleets at once and extracts credentials in place with pypykatz.
tools.when: When you hold admin on a set of Windows hosts and want to audit logged-on credential exposure across the fleet without interactive sessions on each box.

tools.name: PowerView
tools.desc: Pure-PowerShell AD enumerator (PowerSploit) turning LDAP into one-liner cmdlets for users, groups, computers, GPOs, ACLs, shares, and trust maps; also hunts which machines specific users log into and where you have local admin.
tools.when: From a domain-joined PowerShell session when you need fast, scriptable situational awareness without dropping a binary on disk — and to see exactly what attackers enumerate first.

tools.name: PowerUp
tools.desc: PowerSploit module that audits a Windows host for common local privilege-escalation misconfigurations — unquoted service paths, writable service binaries, modifiable services, AlwaysInstallElevated — and reports each with abuse-ready detail.
tools.when: Local privilege-escalation audit of a single host during sanctioned testing or as part of hardening a fleet that lacks LAPS and least-privilege discipline.

tools.name: BloodHound.py
tools.desc: Python/Impacket ingestor for BloodHound CE that collects users, computers, groups, trusts, ACLs, sessions, and local admins from Linux using only credentials — no Windows host or SharpHound binary required.
tools.when: When you need BloodHound data but have no Windows foothold; the Linux-native collection counterpart to SharpHound.
tools.install: pipx install bloodhound-ce (bloodhound-ce branch adds the bloodhound-ce-python CLI)

tools.name: PingCastle
tools.desc: Active Directory risk and maturity audit (by Netwrix) that scores a domain 0–100 across ~10 axes — accounts, ADCS, Kerberos, trusts, delegation, GPOs, infrastructure — and emits a CISO-ready HTML report with prioritized remediation via a read-only healthcheck.
tools.when: The default first formal AD security assessment: minutes to run, zero writes, and ideal as a recurring blue-team health check or engagement kickoff.
tools.install: Download standalone PingCastle.exe from https://github.com/netwrix/pingcastle/releases and run on a domain-joined Windows host (.NET 8)

tools.name: Purple Knight
tools.desc: Free commercial assessment from Semperis scoring hybrid AD, Entra ID, and Okta estates against 150+ indicators of exposure and compromise, with MITRE ATT&CK mapping and prioritized executive guidance.
tools.when: Complement PingCastle when you also manage Entra ID or Okta and want an easy scorecard plus IoC checks across the hybrid estate.
tools.install: Download the Windows agent from https://www.semperis.com/purple-knight/ (free registration required)

tools.name: ADRecon
tools.desc: PowerShell tool that extracts a wide slice of AD state — users, groups, OUs, GPOs, trusts, ACLs, password policies, DNS zones, and optionally LAPS/BitLocker keys and Kerberoastable SPNs — and consolidates it into a summary Excel workbook.
tools.when: Broad read-only documentation of an environment for audit reports; runs as an ordinary domain user and works from non-member hosts over LDAP.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/adrecon/ADRecon && .\ADRecon.ps1 on a Windows host

tools.name: AD-Audit
tools.desc: Modular PowerShell auditing suite aligned to Microsoft security best practices: user/computer hygiene, group policy, domain-controller security, credential-theft prevention, least privilege, AD FS, event monitoring, and ADCS checks with SQLite-backed findings.
tools.when: Teams wanting an extensible, automation-friendly policy-check audit (CI/CD output) rather than a single maturity score.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/adrian207/AD-Audit && Import-Module .\AD-Audit.psd1 (requires PowerShell 5.1+ and the RSAT ActiveDirectory module)
